correctness.rationale: For the nonempty-subset power monoid a central subset commutes with each singleton. If a member sends i to j != i, its right restriction by the singleton-domain identity on i produces an arrow with image j, impossible on the other side. Thus every member is a partial identity. Conjugation by full permutations makes a central subset a union of the rank layers E_r. Conversely, for a partial bijection of rank d, composing on either side with E_r gives exactly its restrictions to u domain points with max(0,r+d-n) <= u <= min(r,d): the chosen r-set is completed outside its domain or outside its image, respectively. Intersection of supports gives the claimed rank multiplication. For 1 <= r < n, the square of E_r contains E_(r-1), forcing downward closure below n for an idempotent; n is an independent identity layer. This gives exactly 2n+1. An intersection of any nonempty family of supports can be realized using at most n members by choosing one missing-point witness for each point outside the intersection (one member if the intersection is full); repeated factors pad to n. Hence A^n = A^(n+1). Exactly n distinct coatoms are required to make the empty intersection, so E_(n-1) proves sharpness for n >= 2; n=1 has exponent one. The subgroup and non-band consequences follow. An independent arrow-set calculation returned (number central, number idempotent, maximal stabilization index) = (3,3,1), (7,5,2), (15,7,3) for n=1,2,3.
residual_risks: The replay is exhaustive over all nonempty subsets only for n=1,2; n=3 exhausts subsets of partial identities after the proved obstruction. Infinite completeness rests on the proof, not the replay.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete center classification for a standard finite inverse monoid. The rank product replaces multiplication of subsets of a large semigroup by rank intervals, gives a complete idempotent census, and yields a best possible aperiodicity identity for the whole center. The distinctive useful fact is the structural reduction to rank supports rather than a small-instance calculation.
residual_risks: Value is specific to the full nonempty-subset power monoid of the finite rook monoid, not a claim about all inverse semigroups or reduced power monoids.
